method: Lines sampled across every scene (night birthday, Anjali/Swamy calls, sister, morning at home, Swamy's family grocery shop, bike ride, tree 'office', Shankaranna's kiosk, Anjali's gift and video call, the delivery-man gag, evening at the tree, home waiting, drunk return, ending), with extra density on 6:08-12:45 where Scribe has a single label. Scribe sentences were split by word times where one sentence holds two speakers. For each line 4 frames evenly spaced over the line (runs/gt/p3XTZlZ6-xw/frames_spk/line_*.jpg, one 4-frame strip per line; sheet_*.jpg stack 3 lines; overview_*.jpg = 1 frame / 12 s; dense_*.jpg = 2 fps for 170, 589, 607, 640, 705, 1139, 1166, 1176, 1246, 1374, 1403, 1530 s; crop_610.jpg and crop_1139.jpg = 4 fps face crops) were checked for who is on screen and whose mouth moves, combined with content (names used, who answers whom, costume continuity). Speaker decided from frames and content; Scribe label (majority word speaker, ties by overlap seconds, as eval.speakers.line_label) added afterwards.

label_conventions.speaker: character name from the list; 'OFFSCREEN:<name>' = the speaker is not visible during the line (other end of a phone call, reaction shot held on a listener, insert shot) but is identified from content/voice context; 'UNKNOWN' = cannot tell. For diarization scoring, strip the OFFSCREEN: prefix.
label_conventions.confidence: 3 = seen speaking and/or unambiguous from content; 2 = likely (wide shot, back to camera or cut mid-line, content supports); 1 = guess
label_conventions.times: seconds in the episode audio; keyed by time, not by Scribe line id
label_conventions.on_screen: everyone visible at any moment during the line (union over frames sampled inside the line's start-end; a cut that lands just outside the line does not count); [] = nobody (an insert shot such as a sign or a phone screen); on_screen_partly = only a back of the head / shoulder / hand / blurred edge is visible (over-the-shoulder foregrounds, a sleeve at the frame edge), not identifiable as a face; a whole figure seen from behind counts as on_screen. Background extras who never speak are not listed; known characters are listed even when silent or small in the background. Independent of speaker: the speaker may be off screen while others are shown. on_screen_note = what was seen, when useful.
label_conventions.voices: only on lines with more than one voice: a list in time order of {from_text: the first word of that voice's part, copied from the line's text, speakers: [names]}; two people one after another = two entries; several people saying it together (group line, everyone laughing a word) = one entry with several names. Lines without voices were checked and have a single voice (clip-gt-editor 2026-11-02: Scribe word speakers inside the line, content, frames; no line in this key needed it).

hard_cases: 6:08-12:45 (shop, bike, tree 'office', Shankaranna's kiosk, Anjali's gift) is one Scribe label (speaker_5) for every speaker: Surya's mother, Swamy, Swamy's father and mother, Surya, Shiva, Shankaranna. All these lines were decided from frames (who faces camera, mouth, gestures) and content (who addresses whom: 'ఏందే' to the wife, 'శంకరన్న', 'మీ అమ్మ').

The delivery man of 15:40-18:45 is Arjun ('V Arjun'/'Virgin') by costume (cap, beard, black jacket over red-navy striped shirt), the same man who rides the bike at night; the customer is a separate unnamed man.

10:08-10:16 (sentences 240-242): Shiva hugs Surya with his back to camera, then a two-shot of Swamy and Surya. Assigned from a 4 fps face crop: 'అయినా పుట్టినరోజు చేసుకోవాలిరా' Shiva (2), 'అవును ఒక్కరోజైనా ఇంట్లో తిట్లు తప్పే కదా' Surya (2), 'ఆ మరుసటి రోజు అవన్నీ cover చేస్తారు కానీ' Swamy (2); 'మీరు continue ఇప్పుడే వస్తా' left UNKNOWN.
11:50 'మనది కాని ఒక్క రూపాయి కూడా మనకొద్దు' is read over an insert of the sign; labelled OFFSCREEN:Shankaranna at confidence 1 (he pointed at it), could be Swamy reading it.
20:50 'సమస్య నీదైనప్పుడు...' is read over the father's phone screen; OFFSCREEN father at confidence 1 (may be the video's own voice).

19:26-19:42 (bar talk) is a wide three-shot with cut-ins on Arjun; Surya's budget lines are assigned by content (his 1000 + 1500), 'virgin' jokes to Swamy because Arjun answers 'రేయ్ స్వామి నువ్వంటావ్ రా'.

Several Scribe sentences hold two speakers and were split by word times: 6:17 'సూర్య ఎక్కడికిరా టిఫిన్ చేయకుండా' (mother) / 'స్వామి దగ్గరికి' (Surya); 6:36 'సబ్బులు ఎన్ని ఉన్నాయాడ' (Swamy's father) / 'ఇరవై ఐదు' (Swamy's mother); 10:12 sentence 242 (Swamy / unknown).
Opening scene (0:14-1:00) is very dark; Meghana / mother / father assigned mainly by content (who wakes whom, 'ఏంటే', 'అండి').

Final line 'నేను జాబ్ తెచ్చుకుంటా' (25:34): the shot is on the father at the door turning back; read as drunk Surya mumbling (OFFSCREEN, 2). Scribe stretches its last word to 26:13 over music; the key line ends at 1535.6 s.
